old: Some linguists trace its root to a word meaning simply "bitter."
In Old English it was spelled ealu, and it named a fermented malt drink.
Scandinavian languages still call beer by a close cousin of this word: öl or øl.
clues: This alcoholic drink has a name that may trace back to an ancient root meaning simply beer, or perhaps bitter.
A kind of beer brewed from fermented malt, usually fuller and fruitier than a crisp lager. Its meaning has barely changed since Old English times.
Its Swedish cousin is öl and its Danish cousin is øl. In a British pub, a pint of the brown or hoppy bitter kind is a classic order.
